To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neural representation of scene category in scene-selective brain areas is more similar between high and full-spectrum images than between high and low spatial images, and that spatial frequency is more explicitly represented in posterior than in anterior PPA.

1) scene-selective visual brain regions are sensitive to the content of spatial frequency information, 2) scene-selective brain activity patterns can be decoded to predict the category of a scene from the content of high spatial frequency information, but not from low spatial frequency information, and 3) the content of spatial-frequency information in the scene is explicitly represented in scene-selective brain areas, specifically the posterior parahippocamal place area (pPPA).
the content of complex natural scenes is predominantly carried by high spatial frequencies, as opposed to low spatial frequencies, in scene-selective brain areas of human observers.
